newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Atletico Madrid studies public share offer.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Atletico Madrid studies public share offer.

text.p: Spanish premier soccer club Atletico Madrid said on Monday it was looking into a possible share float on Madrid's bourse.

"We are studying the possibilities for quoting on the bourse and to this end have contracted a study from a group of institutions," Alvaro Gomez, the club's financial director, told Reuters. "If everything goes well, we could have a public share offer within two years."
Atletico Madrid, which finished fifth in the Spanish league championship in June, contracted BBV Interactivos, Merrill Lynch, HSBC and Apax Partners for the study.
Gomez said the share offer would help strengthen the club financially.
"If possibilities to quote exist, if would be foolishness not to do so, because it would be a very big advantage for the club, particularly when facing new investments," Gomez said.
Atletico Madrid's budget for the current season is almost 5.0 billion pesetas. It had a 400 million peseta profit last season.
